newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan union calls US sanctions "gunboat diplomacy".
newsitem.headline: Japan union calls US sanctions "gunboat diplomacy".

text.p: A Japanese port workers' union said on Thursday that a U.S. decision to impose sanctions on Japanese ships calling at U.S. ports was "gunboat diplomacy".

"If the U.S. has complaints about port practices here, they could have found a solution through consultations. But they resorted directly to sanctions," said a senior official of the National Council of Dock Workers' Unions.
"This is gunboat diplomacy and not democratic," he said.

Two major labour unions -- the National Council of Dock Workers' Unions and the Japan Confederation of Port and Transport Workers' Unions -- have decided to stage a 24-hour protest strike on March 12.
The unions are upset by a U.S. decision to impose sanctions on Japanese ships calling at U.S. ports. The strike would affect operations of container ships docking at all major ports in Japan.

Last week the U.S. Federal Maritime Commission, angry at what it says are costly and discriminatory practices at Japanese ports, said it would slap $100,000 surcharges from April 14 on vessels of Kawasaki Kisen, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines Ltd and Nippon Yusen KK each time they stop at a U.S. port.
